_about: Public-domain Herrick Johnson (1832-1913), Presbyterian minister and professor at McCormick Seminary, Chicago, for the Word Hoard: Christianity's Challenge (1881), Revivals, their Place and their Power (1882), A Plain Talk about the Theater (1882), Forms for Special Occasions (1889), From Love to Praise (1903) and The Ideal Ministry (1908). Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 60 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

hjohnson-christianitys-challenge: Christianity's challenge and some phases of Christianity submitted for candid consideration (New York, American tract soc., 1881)
hjohnson-revivals: Revivals : their place and their power (Chicago : F.H. Revell, 1882)
hjohnson-theater: A plain talk about the theater (Chicago, F. H. Revell, 1882)
hjohnson-special-occasions: Forms for special occasions : marriage, burial, baptism, the Lord's supper, ordination, dedication, etc., with Scripture selections for the chamber of sickness, the house of mourning, the service at funerals (Chicago : C. H. Whiting, 1889)
hjohnson-love-to-praise: From love to praise (Philadelphia, Presbyterian Board of Publication and Sabbath-school work, 1903)
hjohnson-ideal-ministry: The ideal ministry (New York, Chicago [etc.] Fleming H. Revell Company, 1908)

_excluded.hjohnson-other: Douglas W. Johnson's New Mexico geology papers (catalogued under the same name); Civil War thanksgiving sermons, a Lincoln discourse and memorial addresses (short pamphlets)
_excluded.hjohnson-comfort: comfortkath00johnrich: Comfort (1877, signed 'H. J.'); the enlarged 1888 edition names its author as 'Mrs. Herrick Johnson', his wife, so it is not his
